title: Burning and Suppression of Solids — II
fuelDetails: Flat PMMA sheets, cotton/fiberglass blends, extruded rods
variables: Forced oxidizer flow velocity, ambient O₂ concentration (15–23%), solid thickness
sensors: Radiometers, high-resolution color CCD cameras, thermography
summary: Investigated how low-speed airflow drafts (0–55 cm/s) sustain or accelerate solid material combustion in microgravity. Proved that low-speed ventilation—common in ISS cabin ducts—drastically increases flame spread rates compared to quiescent zero-gravity conditions, identifying a critical design hazard for habitat HVAC systems.

title: Spacecraft Fire Safety Demonstration I, II & III
fuelDetails: Large-scale SIBAL fabric (75% cotton, 25% fiberglass), PMMA sheets (up to 1m x 0.4m)
variables: Realistic spacecraft cabin scale, upward vs downward spread, depressurization venting
sensors: Multi-angle video arrays, thermocouples, pressure transducers, O₂/CO₂ gas analyzers
summary: First realistic, large-scale spacecraft fire experiments conducted inside an uncrewed Cygnus resupply vehicle after departing the ISS. Tested flame spread over 1-meter-long solid fabric panels, establishing definitive empirical boundary conditions for rapid cabin fire growth, toxic gas generation, and depressurization dynamics.

title: Coflow Flames in Inverted & Partial Gravity
fuelDetails: Methane / Ethylene / Nitrogen coflow gas burners
variables: Partial-gravity emulated buoyant flows, oxidizer enrichment up to 85% O₂, strain rates
sensors: PLIF laser diagnostics, soot emission spectrometers, chemiluminescence
summary: Groundbreaking study mapping combustion behavior across simulated partial-gravity regimes (lunar 0.16g and Martian 0.38g). Discovered that at intermediate partial gravities, flames transition into uniquely unstable, oscillating modes where flammability limits expand—making materials burn at lower oxygen thresholds than either on Earth or in zero-g.

title: Burning Rate Emulator
fuelDetails: Porous flat & cylindrical burners emulating PMMA, polyethylene, and cellulose fuels
variables: Surface heat flux, mass transfer driving force (B-number), O₂ fraction (15–35%)
sensors: Radiative heat flux radiometers, burner surface thermistors, chemiluminescence cameras
summary: Emulated solid fuel burning physics using gas-fed porous burners to decouple solid-phase thermal degradation from gas-phase chemical kinetics. Provided the fundamental transfer-number (B-number) flammability metrics required to construct predictive NASA flammability models for lunar habitat atmospheres.

title: Flame Extinguishment Experiment & Cool Flames
rackFull: Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) + Multi-user Droplet Combustion Apparatus (MDCA)
fuelDetails: Heptane, decane, and alcohol single/binary fuel droplets (1.5–5.0 mm dia)
variables: CO₂ and Helium suppressant dilution ratios, droplet diameter, ambient pressure, radiative loss
sensors: Backlit droplet sizing camera, UV/IR radiometers, PLIF/chemiluminescence optics
summary: Studied how CO₂ and Helium inert gas dilution extinguish spherical microgravity droplet flames. Made the breakthrough discovery of invisible low-temperature 'Cool Flames' (500–800 K) that continue burning after visible radiative extinction and can trigger explosive hot re-ignition.

title: Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment & Reflight
fuelDetails: Pyrolyzed Teflon, Kapton, silicone, and Nomex wire insulation & circuit boards
variables: Microgravity vs terrestrial soot agglomeration, primary particle diameter (10–1000 nm)
sensors: Differential Mobility Analyzer (DMA), condensation particle counters, transmission electron microscopy
summary: Proved that space smoke particles agglomerate into significantly larger, fluffy chain-like clusters in microgravity due to absence of buoyant separation. Revealed that standard terrestrial ionization smoke detectors fail or trigger late on spacecraft, mandating next-generation multi-wavelength optical obscuration systems.

title: Electric-Field Effects on Microgravity Flames
fuelDetails: Methane / Ethylene diluted with Nitrogen gas
variables: High-voltage DC/AC electric fields (-10 kV to +10 kV), ion wind momentum transfer
sensors: Intensified CCD flame cameras, voltage/current logging, soot laser extinction
summary: Demonstrated that applying external electric fields generates an 'ionic wind' that deflects, controls, and rapidly extinguishes flames in microgravity without using any chemical suppressant agents or liquid water, opening a radical pathway for solid-state electrical fire suppression in long-duration habitats.

title: Dust and Aerosol Measurement Feasibility Test
fuelDetails: Simulated lunar regolith dust simulant (JSC-1A) blended with combustion soot
variables: Mineral dust vs carbonaceous smoke discrimination, optical scatter ratios
sensors: P-Trak ultrafine particle counter, DustTrak photometers, optical particle counters
summary: Addressed the vital challenge of distinguishing abrasive lunar surface dust from early-stage smoldering wire insulation smoke in Artemis habitat airlocks. Established optical dual-wavelength scattering signatures to eliminate false fire alarms triggered by tracked-in regolith.

title: Smoke Point In Co-flow Experiment / Structure & Liftoff
fuelDetails: Ethylene, propane, and methane gas laminar jet diffusion flames
variables: Soot inception limit, fuel flow rate at smoke point, flame liftoff height
sensors: Color video camera, radiometers, soot thermophoretic sampling pins
summary: Quantified the soot emission threshold ('smoke point') for laminar flames in microgravity. Proved that microgravity flames emit significantly more soot and unburned hydrocarbons at lower fuel flow rates than terrestrial flames due to longer residence times and absence of buoyant acceleration.

title: Lunar Combustion Investigation / Flammability Map
rackFull: Artemis Lunar Surface & Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS)
fuelDetails: Artemis lunar outpost composite materials, EVA suit fabric swatches, 3D printed regolith binders
variables: True 1/6th lunar gravity, 34% O₂ at 8.2 psi Exploration Atmosphere, dust presence
sensors: Multi-spectral radiometers, laser extinction, micro-thermocouple arrays
summary: Next-generation investigation designed to establish the definitive flammability map directly on the lunar surface under Artemis. Bridges the critical gap between orbital drop-tower/centrifuge simulations and long-term uncrewed lunar surface fire physics.
